justifications.durability: The guard is real and falsifiable: removing the mask reddens four of the seven tests (verified against the recorded negative-control log, and reproduced by the mutation mechanism -- an all-false mask makes triangles_outside_wall return False everywhere, so the drawn vertices leave the wall, the mask flags nothing, and the all-outside ValueError never fires). The new test is default-collected, so the painter's contract is pinned. Held below 20 because the repository still carries the ~40 renderers the followup names that draw outside the wall with no guard that a caller passes wall=, and no test asserts that the raster-blanking path leaves the vessel interior's contour coverage intact alongside the blanking.
justifications.evidence: Held below 20 because the reviewed run recorded no base arm even though its own done-when says 'no failure is added, against a stated base' -- it argued the change additive rather than measuring it. I measured it: base d598cd193 (review tree, whose nova/media/poloidal.py blob 6c860029 equals base) and head d4f4c723f (target worktree) each ran the same six nova.media-importing modules in their own fresh process and both are green with zero failures, so added_failure_count is 0 by a measured head-minus-base set identity, not by assertion. The negative control is recorded and reddens for the claimed reason (below). The one head arm the run could not finish, test_playable_session, hit its 540 s bound with no failure seen and is an incomplete measurement, not a pass.
justifications.fit: The implementation reuses inside_wall_units and the wall-unit collection draw_wall already reads (no second wall representation, as the measure requires), names by mechanism (triangles_outside_wall, draw_scattered_contours), and carries no plan, sprint or ticket identifier in any symbol, filename or comment; the fragment cites the followup id as required. No abstraction beyond the two helpers and one optional keyword. Minor: the new wall parameter is the only unannotated argument on draw_scattered_contours.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The goal and followup f-fsa-painters-draw-field-outside-the-wall asks that scattered-node triangulations be masked to the wall and a test added that fails when a drawn contour vertex lies outside the polygon. The node adds draw_scattered_contours and triangles_outside_wall (masks a triangle unless its centroid, three vertices and three edge midpoints are all inside the wall units -- a strict superset of the requested centroid rule, so it cannot draw outside where the requested rule would not), adds an optional wall= to draw_flux_contours that blanks grid points outside the units, and ships tests/test_contour_inside_wall.py. It does not edit the benchmark renderers the followup also names (its fence was nova/media/poloidal.py plus the test); instead it equips callers to opt in and lists those renderers by file and line in the report, which is the correct handling for an out-of-fence caller change.

The report is written to the run-scoped reports directory the fence names. No concurrent node's path is touched.

notes: The reviewed node masks scattered-node contour triangulations to the first wall. The code is a clean, additive repair: draw_scattered_contours masks any triangle not wholly inside the wall units (a superset of the requested centroid rule, so it cannot draw outside where the rule would not) and draw_flux_contours gains an optional wall= that blanks grid points outside the units; both reuse inside_wall_units and the draw_wall unit collection with no second wall model. The new test is default-collected and its guard is falsifiable -- the recorded negative control (mask removed) reddens 4 of 7 with 13 of 443 drawn vertices outside the wall. Scope is exactly the three declared paths.
